items.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023
items.q: Lalo Schifrin — I mean Michel Legrand it was

ctx.x: Isn’t it amazing that those gentlemen, especially the black musicians who went through so much trial over the years, still had that life force that you — as you describe like sitting next to them for a couple of hours, like you just feel better afterwards.

Oh jeez, it’s heaven. It’s heavenly I mean it really was. Wow. I mean I never thought that would happen. And then Miles Davis, another one. I saw him in New York. You know we didn’t get to hang, it was a different situation. That was when I did the album “Dingo” with Miles. Do you know that album? And the story, and he was in the movie you know. And when I did that I had to be some — when you mentioned I had to be somebody you know, Lalo Schifrin — I mean Michel Legrand it was, and I go into the studio to do this…

him in New York, going back to New York and the Village, and once again it was a very brief meeting. I sat down next to him in a bar, or he came in, I was at the bar. We were in back with the orchestra with Jack Elliott and Allyn Ferguson. And we did it live at Studio 8H in New York. So we got there and got to the Village when we flew in and everything was closing. But we went into this one place, we went into the Brecker Brothers’ club and that was closed. They were all closed already. But this one club in the…
